tasks.name: Design secure access to AWS resources

concepts.name: Shared responsibility and root-user hygiene
concepts.description: AWS secures the cloud infrastructure, while customers secure their data, identities, configurations, and workloads in the cloud.

concepts.name: IAM policies and explicit deny
concepts.description: IAM authorization evaluates applicable identity and resource policies, and an explicit Deny overrides an Allow.

concepts.name: IAM roles, STS, and cross-account access
concepts.description: IAM roles provide temporary credentials and are commonly assumed through AWS STS instead of using long-term access keys.

concepts.name: IAM Identity Center and federation
concepts.description: AWS IAM Identity Center centralizes workforce access to multiple AWS accounts and applications by using federated identities and permission sets.

concepts.name: Organizations, SCPs, and Control Tower
concepts.description: AWS Organizations groups accounts, SCPs set permission guardrails, and AWS Control Tower helps establish and govern a multi-account landing zone.

concepts.name: Resource-based policies
concepts.description: Resource-based policies attach to supported AWS resources and can name principals that are allowed or denied access.

concepts.name: Permissions boundaries
concepts.description: A permissions boundary sets the maximum permissions that an IAM user or role can receive from identity-based policies.

concepts.name: VPC segmentation: public and private tiers
concepts.description: A subnet is public when its route table provides a path to an internet gateway; private application and database tiers normally avoid direct inbound internet paths.

concepts.name: Security groups vs network ACLs
concepts.description: Security groups are stateful controls attached to resources such as ENIs, while network ACLs are stateless controls applied at the subnet boundary.

concepts.name: VPC endpoints and AWS PrivateLink
concepts.description: VPC endpoints provide private access to supported services without requiring traffic to traverse an internet gateway or NAT gateway.

concepts.name: Secrets Manager
concepts.description: AWS Secrets Manager stores sensitive credentials and supports controlled retrieval and automated rotation for supported secret types.

concepts.name: AWS WAF and AWS Shield
concepts.description: AWS WAF filters HTTP and HTTPS requests with web ACL rules, while AWS Shield provides managed protection against distributed denial-of-service attacks.

concepts.name: GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and Security Hub
concepts.description: GuardDuty detects suspicious activity, Inspector identifies software and network exposure vulnerabilities, Macie discovers sensitive data in S3, and Security Hub aggregates security findings.

concepts.name: KMS encryption and key policies
concepts.description: AWS KMS creates and controls encryption keys that AWS services can use to protect data at rest.

concepts.name: ACM and encryption in transit
concepts.description: AWS Certificate Manager provisions and manages TLS certificates for supported integrated AWS services.

concepts.name: S3 access, versioning, lifecycle, and Object Lock
concepts.description: Amazon S3 combines IAM and bucket policies with features such as versioning, lifecycle rules, replication, and Object Lock to control access and protect object data.

concepts.name: Backup and replication controls
concepts.description: Backups create recoverable copies, while replication maintains additional copies in another location for availability, locality, or disaster-recovery objectives.

concepts.name: Data classification and governance
concepts.description: Data classification identifies sensitive or regulated information so that access, encryption, retention, and monitoring controls can match the data's requirements.
